Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

ios.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is -5.4% and App Total Install is +4.5%; the gap between them (-9.9pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — All App is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-6.5% vs Install +2.1%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: All App New Subs -6.5% vs Install +2.1% (worse than its installs); YMK New Subs -10.3% vs Install +3.8% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Revenue -7.3% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Revenue moved -7.3% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -7.3%, YMK -0.3%, YCP -15.7%, YCV -14.8%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total New Subs (+3.7% vs -6.5%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total New Subs in US is +3.7% while all countries together are -6.5% — a gap of +10.1pp. US is about 43% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting toward SEO Install (+21.1% vs +2.1% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 2,165, +21.1% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved +2.1% — a difference of +19.0 percentage points. SEO Install is now 6.6% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -10.2% matches the new subs signed up 7 days earlier.
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 10-10 vs 10-03 is -10.2%, and App Total New Subs on 10-03 vs 09-26 was -14.3% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

insights.title: Best and worst markets — CA turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (19.3% vs 11.4% overall).
insights.body: In CA, 19.3% of installs turn into new subs, versus 11.4% across all markets and apps (+7.8pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. CA is about 2% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -14.0% this period.

insights.title: Market trend — YCP is gaining ground fast on turning installs into subs (+31.3%, now 11.8%).
insights.body: In YCP, 11.8% of installs now turn into new subs — +31.3% versus last period. It is about 37% of revenue (a big revenue market): more of the people downloading are subscribing, which should help revenue within a week or two.
